newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan electronics shares rise on overseas orders.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan electronics shares rise on overseas orders.

text.p: Taiwan's electronics sector continued its bull run, rising sharply at mid-morning on Tuesday in defiance of central bank moves to cool the red-hot stock market, brokers said.
With 74 minutes remaining at 0246 GMT, the sector was up 2.27 percent, strongly outpacing the broad index, which was up just 0.53 percent.

Encouraged by Monday's local gains and a sharp overnight rally in Wall Street's high-tech sector, Taiwan investors rushed to lay in electronic shares, while others were holding onto what they already had, brokers said.
"The electronic sector is too strong to be shaken by any market-dampening moves by the central bank," said National Securities analyst Virginia Tsai.
Most high-tech firms had issued strong earnings reports in the second quarter, she said, forecasting that the electronic uptrend should continue at least for two more weeks.

Brokers said the sector was expected to make strong third-quarter gains as a number of firms, including computer makers Acer and Mitac, had recently received large commercial orders from U.S. and European buyers.
